summary: When loading a world, the held item from the previously loaded world is briefly visible
description:
This happens in Singleplayer, any gamemode, especially on lower render distance.

Expected:

When loading a world, your hand should be holding the thing currently selected in the hotbar.

Actually seen:

Your hand starts out (briefly) holding the thing selected in the hotbar in the last world you were in, then it does the item-switching animation (lower hand holding previous item, raise hand now holding current item).

It's quick, so to reproduce it, try a few times.

Steps:

1) Have 2 worlds created.

2) In one world, select something from the hotbar so it's held in-hand, e.g. lime wool.

3) Save and quit, open the other world. Select something else in-hand, e.g. nether brick.

4) Save and quit, open the first world again. Your hand will lower the nether brick, and raise the lime wool.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open Singleplayer and create or use two Creative worlds.
2. Enter the first world.
3. Select lime wool in the hotbar so it is held in-hand.
4. Open the Esc menu and select Save and Quit to Title.
5. Open the second world.
6. Select nether brick in the hotbar so it is held in-hand.
7. Open the Esc menu and select Save and Quit to Title.
8. Open the first world again.
9. Wait until the first world finishes loading.
10. Observe that the hand briefly lowers while holding nether brick, then raises while holding lime wool.
Observed Behavior:
### Actual behavior

When entering a world in singleplayer, the first-person hand briefly renders the item that was selected in the hotbar in the previously loaded world. It then plays the normal item-switch animation: the previously displayed item is lowered and the item selected in the newly loaded world is raised into view.

The incorrect item is visible only briefly during world loading, but the issue can be reproduced across game modes and is more noticeable when using a lower render distance.
Expected Behavior: When loading a world, the player’s hand should immediately display the item currently selected in that world’s hotbar. The item held in the previously loaded world should not appear, even briefly, and no item-switching animation should lower or raise the hand during world loading. This behavior should remain consistent across singleplayer game modes and render-distance settings.
